rv.q: Gradually, the play reveals itself as a touching celebration of enduring love, family and forgiveness.
It is what it is: a slightly soppy, unfashionable play whose 90 years are showing.
A gorgeous evening that deserves to spread its tentacles further than this limited run.

cn.t: Dodie Smith's 1938 family drama receives a timely, poignant revival anchored by Lindsay Duncan's superb performance. Critics find the old-fashioned play surprisingly resonant, with its melancholy tone reflecting contemporary anxieties.
